answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a random deep-audit lottery. Every epoch, the network selects a small random sample of identities for a full review of their history and counterparties; any identity caught faking loses all standing and stake. Selection is random and unbuyable, so a farm cannot shield its fakes. Like a glacier over shale, the audit grinds false foundations to dust, leaving only identities with real history standing, dark and solid as sable. Each extra fake is another ticket for total loss, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
